intro: Ask around for the hotel in Nong Khai town that gets location, cleanliness and views right, and Amanta Hotel Nongkhai is the name guests mention most · A 4-star hotel opened in 2016 on Kaew Worawut Road in the city centre, it is a short walk to the Mekong riverfront and Tha Sadet market · Rooms are clean and have balconies, there is a pool and a koi pond in the garden, but the real draw is the rooftop sky bar and restaurant looking across the Mekong to Laos at sunset · Guests rate it highly for breakfast and service · From approx ฿1,300/night.

body.html: Amanta Hotel Nongkhai has been open since 2016, sitting on Kaew Worawut Road in the centre of Nong Khai town, an easy walk to the Mekong riverfront and Tha Sadet market · It is a fairly small property of around 33 rooms, which keeps the mood quiet and the service attentive · The thing guests notice as they walk in is the small garden with its koi pond and fountain, which feels far greener and calmer than the usual block-style town hotel.

Rooms range from Superior and Deluxe up to a Suite · Almost every room has a private balcony, and several guests suggest asking for one that faces the garden or pond for a nicer outlook · Rooms are warm-toned with comfortable beds, flat-screen TVs, a fridge, a safe and good hot-water pressure · The most common praise is for cleanliness and the well-kept bathrooms · The occasional complaint is a slight musty smell in some rooms on arrival, mostly ground-floor rooms near the garden, but staff sort it out quickly when asked.
"Clean room, lovely staff, and in the evening we went up to the sky bar to watch the sun set over the Mekong, looking across to Laos — easily the best view of our whole Nong Khai trip."

What sets Amanta apart from other hotels in town is the rooftop sky bar and restaurant · In the evening it is where guests head for a drink looking across the Mekong to Laos, and the sunset view earns plenty of praise in reviews · There is also an outdoor pool, a gym and free parking on site · Breakfast is another high point guests mention — a buffet with both international dishes and local Isan food, tasty and varied even though the hotel itself is small.

Location is the clear advantage here · The hotel is central, within walking distance of Tha Sadet market and the Mekong riverfront, surrounded by restaurants, cafés and souvenir shops · Wat Pho Chai (home of the revered Luang Pho Phra Sai) and the Sala Kaew Ku sculpture park are a short drive away, and the Thai–Lao Friendship Bridge is about 10–15 minutes by car, which makes it handy as a base before crossing to Vientiane · The trade-off is that the hotel does not sit right on the river — you have to walk out a little to reach the waterfront, though it is not far.

Honestly, Amanta Hotel Nongkhai suits anyone who wants a clean, well-run town hotel with a Mekong view at a reasonable price · If you are in Nong Khai for the temples, the riverfront, or as a stopover before crossing to Laos, it fits the bill nicely · A score of 9.3 from 209 Trip.com reviews and consistently strong ratings on Booking.com show that most guests come away pleased · The grumbles you do see are about the musty smell in some rooms and a building that is starting to show its age, but overall it is well maintained.

A tip from reading the reviews: ask for a higher floor facing the garden or pond, and do not miss the sky bar at sunset, which is when the Mekong view is at its best · If you are travelling during the Naga Fireball festival or the end of Buddhist Lent, book well ahead — hotels in central Nong Khai fill up fast · Driving in is easy thanks to the free on-site parking.

honestSummary: Amanta Hotel Nongkhai sells a central location, cleanliness and a sky bar over the Mekong — a short walk to the riverfront and Tha Sadet market, with a pool and a leafy koi-pond garden and warm service, ideal for temple visits, riverfront wandering and travellers stopping over before crossing to Laos · The trade-offs are a musty smell in some rooms and a building that is starting to age.
honestChecks: If you want a room right on the Mekong with a river view from your window — this hotel is in the city centre and you walk out a little to reach the waterfront → if the in-room view matters most, pick a property that sits directly on the river.

If you are particular about a brand-new building — the hotel has been open since 2016 and shows some wear in places, with a musty smell in a few rooms → ask to change rooms at check-in if yours is not right.
If you visit during the Naga Fireball festival or end of Lent — central Nong Khai hotels fill up fast and prices climb → book well ahead and lock in a free-cancellation rate.

faqTitle: Frequently asked questions — Amanta Hotel Nongkhai

faq.q: Where is Amanta Hotel Nongkhai and how do I get there?
faq.a: It is at 999 Moo 1, Kaew Worawut Road, in central Nong Khai · You can walk to the Mekong riverfront and Tha Sadet market · Wat Pho Chai (Luang Pho Phra Sai) and Sala Kaew Ku are about 5–10 minutes by car · The Thai–Lao Friendship Bridge is around 10–15 minutes by car, making it a handy base before crossing to Vientiane · There is free on-site parking.

faq.q: How much does Amanta Hotel Nongkhai cost and what rooms are available?
faq.a: Rates start from about ฿1,300/night for a Superior room · Deluxe King and Deluxe Twin rooms run roughly ฿1,500–฿1,600, and the more spacious Suite around ฿2,400 · Almost every room has a private balcony · Prices vary by season and package, so compare a few platforms before booking.

faq.q: Does Amanta Hotel Nongkhai have a rooftop bar and a pool?
faq.a: Yes to both · The rooftop sky bar and restaurant look across the Mekong to Laos and are a popular spot for sunset · There is an outdoor pool, a gym and a leafy koi-pond garden on site, which gives a calmer feel than the usual block-style town hotel.

faq.q: What are the rooms like at Amanta Hotel Nongkhai — are they clean?
faq.a: Rooms are warm-toned with comfortable beds and almost every room has a private balcony, plus a flat-screen TV, fridge, safe and good hot-water pressure · Guests praise the cleanliness and well-kept bathrooms · A few reviews mention a slight musty smell on arrival, mainly in ground-floor rooms, but staff fix it quickly when asked.

faq.q: Who is Amanta Hotel Nongkhai best for?
faq.a: It suits anyone who wants a clean, well-run town hotel with a Mekong view at a reasonable price · Good for temple visits, riverfront wandering, couples, families and travellers stopping over before crossing to Laos · Handy for self-drivers thanks to free parking.

faq.q: What should I know before booking Amanta Hotel Nongkhai?
faq.a: The hotel does not sit directly on the Mekong — you walk out a little to reach the waterfront · It has been open since 2016 and shows some wear in places, with a musty smell in a few rooms, so ask to change at check-in if yours is not right · Rooms fill fast during the Naga Fireball festival and end of Lent, so book well ahead.
